body.t: Mail needs USPS's ZIP; demographics need Census's ZCTA. This page hands you both, labelled — the
A form's ZIP and the point's ZCTA disagreeing slightly is normal geography, not an error — the page explains your own address to you.
ZCTAs are how the Census publishes ZIP-scale statistics. Defining a study area starts with knowing which ZCTA truly contains your points.
Carriers route by USPS ZIP. When a delivery misroutes, comparing the two labels is the first diagnostic.
USPS ZIPs are delivery routes — lines and points that change for mail efficiency. ZCTAs are Census-built areas approximating ZIP coverage for statistics. Neighbours mostly, twins never.
The ZCTA view joins recent ACS estimates for the area — population-scale context for the exact geography researchers actually use.

faq: Is a Census ZCTA the same thing as a USPS ZIP Code?
No — cousins, not twins. ZIPs are USPS delivery routes; ZCTAs are Census statistical areas built to approximate them. This page shows both separately for exactly that reason.
Which value should I use for mailing?
The USPS ZIP — the address postcode shown. Mail follows the Postal Service's geography, full stop.
Why might the postcode and ZCTA differ?
Because routes and areas diverge at edges: a ZIP can serve addresses across a ZCTA boundary, and some ZIPs (PO boxes, single facilities) have no ZCTA at all.
Where do the demographic statistics come from?
The Census Bureau's American Community Survey — recent estimates for the ZCTA, shown as estimates with their vintage.
Can I search or use GPS?
Both — address search, GPS, coordinates and clicks all resolve to the point whose two labels are then read.
PO Box ZIPs?
They exist as USPS ZIPs with no territory; the ZCTA side of the page will show the surrounding area's tabulation instead — a perfect specimen of the distinction.
New ZIP codes?
USPS creates and retires ZIPs continuously; Census ZCTAs update on Census cycles. A fresh ZIP may briefly outrun its ZCTA twin.
ZIP+4?
The +4 refines delivery segments within USPS data — beyond this page's scope; USPS's own lookup owns that grain.
Is the ZCTA boundary official for anything legal?
It is official Census geography for statistics. Legal and mailing questions belong to their own authorities (USPS, county, courts).
ZIP for a highway point?
No address, maybe no ZIP — ZIPs serve addresses and boxes. The ZCTA side may still answer for the area; the pair shows which kind of nothing you have.
Uniquely-coded facilities?
Some single-building ZIPs (a famous HQ, a university) have no ZCTA — the page's two labels diverge exactly as designed there.
